bio: 1967年生于益子，濱田窑第三代当主，也是濱田庄司的外孙。其创作与研究工作延续益子传统的柿釉、黑釉、白釉、青釉与赤绘体系，同时通过展览和驻留活动把濱田家工艺传统转译到国际观众面前。作为今日益子传统釉药系统的重要维护者，他在工房与研究馆两端都承担关键角色。1967年生，活动重心与栃木県芳賀郡益子町相关，主要于濱田窯作陶，以益子传统釉药、柿釉、黑釉、白釉、赤绘为主要创作方向。其履历中可确认的成就包括濱田庄司孙子、濱田晋作次子。代表发表记录可见于2024年“濱田家三代展”（日本全国）。
style: 益子传统釉药、柿釉、黑釉、白釉、赤绘

bio: Kazuaki Shimura, born in 1980 and now based in Minamiboso, is a Japanese potter whose current practice follows training periods in Kyoto, Ishikawa, and Mashiko. Public profile and retail material consistently describe warm, table-oriented vessels intended to raise the emotional temperature of daily living. While his studio is now outside the four priority regions, his Kyoto and Mashiko training lineage plus follower count make him a pragmatic addition to the discovery dataset.

bio: 1976年生于山梨，东京国分寺「由木窑」主理，日本工艺协会正会员，Instagram粉丝约11.4K。发展"练继/绞胎拼接"技法与粉红色调表达，使用瓷土与多材料混合。作品以器物与陶艺造型为主，日本工艺协会展多次获奖，展现出对练继技法的独特理解与色彩表现力。1976年生，活动重心与東京都国分寺市相关，主要于由木窯作陶，以发展"练继/绞胎拼接"技法与粉红色调表达；使用瓷土与多材料混合为主要创作方向。其履历中可确认的成就包括2013年日本传统工艺展日本工艺协会奖励奖。代表发表记录可见于2024年“磁器展”（东京柿傳画廊）。
style: 发展"练继/绞胎拼接"技法与粉红色调表达；使用瓷土与多材料混合

bio: Kousuke Teramura, born in 1978 in Kyoto and now working in Mashiko, is a contemporary Japanese ceramic artist whose profile links Kyoto training history with an established Mashiko production base. Public media, retail, and profile sources describe a practice centered on practical vessels, calm natural colors, and the tactile balance between clay body and glaze surface. He is especially useful for this discovery task because he strengthens the underrepresented Mashiko quota while already exceeding the Instagram follower requirement.

bio: Midori Uchida, born in 1983 in Kobe, studied ceramics at Osaka University of Arts and completed the Tajimi City Pottery Design and Technical Center program before establishing her practice in Gifu. Gallery material consistently emphasizes carbonization firing, hand-built unglazed forms, and an interest in capturing inner landscapes through kiln phenomena. Her exhibition record shows sustained visibility in Gifu, Tokyo, Kyoto, and art-fair contexts, making her a strong female candidate aligned with the task card’s contemporary focus.
